### Scatter chart
One measure plotted against another, with a point for each row.

Component ID: `scatter-chart`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Weight against city and highway fuel economy for twenty cars is a scatter chart. Fuel economy by model year is a line chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-24); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-24, `llm.md#scatter-chart`): Points drawn from a figure's data table, with a shared x column and one series per further column, gaps for cells that are not numbers, fixed ranges for both scales, round labels for both scales with .axis, a legend with .toggle, update() motion, data-watch, a pointer and keyboard tooltip that steps through points in table order, and .bubble sizes from the last column with areas proportional to its values.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the SVG is aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: Point placement in left-to-right and right-to-left pages, gaps, both axes, the tooltip, keyboard steps, the nearest point by pointer, update() motion, data-watch, the toggle legend and .bubble areas, gaps, tooltip, refit and size motion are checked in a browser; screen reader output, forced colors and enlarged text remain unverified. There are no trend lines, separate x columns per series or sizes per series.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#scatter-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="scatter-chart">` takes a `<figcaption>` and a `<table>`. The first column labels each row, the second holds its x value, and each further column is a series of y values named by its header cell. `AutoInit()` draws one point per series for each row, at the row's x value and the series' y value. A legend names the series when there are two or more, and a tooltip shows the point under the pointer. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="scatter-chart axis" data-x-min="0">
  <figcaption>Fuel economy by weight</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Car</th><th>Weight (kg)</th><th>City mpg</th><th>Highway mpg</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Civic</th><td>1300</td><td>31</td><td>40</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Camry</th><td>1600</td><td>28</td><td>39</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Tahoe</th><td>2600</td><td>15</td><td>20</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

The Scatter chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `scatter-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .scatter-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `scatter-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .scatter-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
